newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Mobutu risks extradition if flees Zaire into exile.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu risks extradition if flees Zaire into exile.

text.p: If embattled ruler Mobutu Sese Seko flees Zaire, he risks being extradited back to his country to stand trial for alleged theft of public property, delegates at a conference on central Africa said on Friday.

"If a new Zairean government could build a case against Mobutu, they could ask for his extradition," J. Victor da Silva Angelo, U.N. resident representative in Tanzania, said after a two-day conference in Lisbon on the African Great Lakes region.
"If no extradition treaty exists between Zaire and the country where Mobutu seeks exile, it becomes a bilateral issue open to negotiation," he said.
"People who appropriate collective goods should be tried," he added.
Mobutu Sese Seko, fighting cancer and seven months of civil war, left his capital Kinshasa on Friday for his northern jungle palace at Gbadolite on doctors' orders, state television said.
But the departure of the man who has dominated Africa's third largest country for more than three decades triggered intense speculation that he was on his way into exile.

His departure followed talks with army chiefs who told him they could not defend the capital against Laurent Kabila's advancing rebel forces and that he should leave for his own safety, political and diplomatic sources in Zaire said.
In Lisbon, Hans-Peter Furrer, director of political affairs of the Council of Europe, said no international court presently had the right to try Mobutu.
"There is no international tribunal that would be competent for that," he said.
Tito Rutaremara, a member of Rwanda's parliament, said: "The world should take steps to set up an international tribunal to try Mobutu, otherwise this encourages impunity."
Mobutu, 66, has reputedly amassed a huge personal fortune since he seized power in 1965.
Switzerland ordered a freeze on Friday on Mobutu's villa but not on other assets, estimated to total $4 billion by Swiss media.

A Swiss government statement said the public prosecutor of the rebel-held Zairean town of Lubumbashi, who asked Switzerland to freeze Mobutu's assets, "appears to be a competent representative of the Zairean judicial authorities."
